headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: opik has broad network egress and REST API access, while LightZero is local-only; other pairwise risks are mostly blocked by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. LightZero has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, and opik only exposes REST API/network egress, so there is no plausible default path for opik content to inject instructions into LightZero or vice versa.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator manually copies opik output into LightZero prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no copy-paste bridge.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik's broad network egress and REST API surface create a default exfiltration path if it receives sensitive inputs, while LightZero is local-only and does not itself leak data. The pair still poses leakage risk because opik can transmit whatever context it is given; LightZero does not add a second leak path.
conditions: IF sensitive files or prompts are fed into opik, they can leave the local environment over the network.
IF LightZero is used only locally with no shared data, leakage risk remains limited.
mitigations: Do not send secrets or regulated data to opik.
Restrict opik to redacted inputs only.
Use a network egress allowlist for opik.
Separate any sensitive workspace from opik's runtime.
requires-engineering: add DLP or content filtering before API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping mutable resource. LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, while opik's documented surface is REST API access with broad egress; without shared write targets or locks, the pair has no capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only.
Avoid giving opik write access to shared repos.
Use separate working directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not documented, and LightZero is a game-playing system rather than an action-taking agent. opik can consume API data, but there is no evidence it treats LightZero outputs as authoritative or that either agent can directly execute downstream actions, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF opik is configured to trust LightZero outputs without verification, error propagation increases.
IF a downstream workflow turns opik outputs into actions, the risk becomes larger.
mitigations: Require human review of LightZero-derived outputs.
Add validation checks before opik consumes model outputs.
Log and sample outputs for spot checks.
Keep action-taking workflows disabled.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any downstream automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy gap is documented for either agent. LightZero touches no data classes and opik lists no secrets handled or special compliance surfaces, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into opik's inputs, compliance review is needed.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy, reassess residency and retention.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future data-class handling.
Review retention settings before deployment.
